channel.title: Global Supply Chain Bulletin
channel.description: An independent daily briefing on supply chains, energy transition and trade geopolitics.

item.title: Issue 97 — UK to send Typhoon jets on defensive missions to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: Euronews and Al Jazeera report Britain’s Typhoon jets will fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia, as IMF PortWatch shows Bab-el-Mandeb transits holding near 26.4 a day, about a third of 2023 levels, with no Houthi response reported.

item.title: Issue 96 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Euronews and Al Jazeera report Britain will fly Typhoon jets on defensive missions to shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks, as IMF PortWatch shows Bab-el-Mandeb transits near 26.4 a day, about a third of 2023 levels.

item.title: Issue 95 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Axios, AP and Business Standard report Trump's Oct 16 Russia sanctions waiver kept drawing bipartisan anger into Oct 19, with Brent crude slipping to $108.17 a barrel on expectations of more Russian fuel reaching market before steadying near $110 Oct 20 (Trading Economics).

item.title: Issue 94 — Trump's Russia sanctions waiver draws instant bipartisan backlash in Congress
item.description: Axios and Business Standard report Trump's Oct 16 waiver of new Russia sanctions drew instant bipartisan anger in Congress, with Rubio telling Al Arabiya and Reuters a permanent decision could take up to 60 days.

item.title: Issue 93 — Trump waives new Russia and Iran sanctions days before the October 18 deadline, citing national interest
item.description: The Associated Press, Axios and Deutsche Welle report Trump waived new Russia and Iran sanctions just two days before their Oct 18 deadline, citing the national interest, while Reuters and Bloomberg report the Bank of Canada warned of sharply higher inflation as oil prices surge.

item.title: Issue 92 — Africa Finance Corporation eyes iron-ore and uranium investments as South Africa launches a $541 million rail upgrade
item.description: Africa Finance Corporation is targeting fresh iron-ore and uranium financing across the continent as South Africa's Transnet began a $541 million upgrade of its iron-ore export railway, Mining Weekly, Mining.com.au and Ecofin Agency report, while major container carriers signal a full return to the Suez Canal by the first quarter of 2027, Hellenic Shipping News and Seatrade Maritime report.

item.title: Issue 91 — IMF warns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia could worsen its economic contraction after Aramco HQ strike
item.description: Houthi missiles killed several officials in a strike on Yemen's Aden presidential palace Thursday, Reuters, Deutsche Welle, Al Jazeera and the South China Morning Post report, as the IMF's pre-strike forecast already puts Saudi Arabia's 2026 GDP contraction at 3.3% after missiles hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, Euronews, Bloomberg and the Associated Press report.

item.title: Issue 90 — Fuel delivery delays trigger panic buying and hour-long queues across Bali
item.description: Indonesia's resort island of Bali faced hour-long fuel queues and panic buying on Oct 14, Africanews, Euronews and the Straits Times report, as Nikkei Asia reports the shortage has spread to other regions with pump prices climbing.

item.title: Issue 89 — France boards another Russia-linked 'shadow fleet' tanker; Moscow calls it 'piracy'
item.description: The Financial Times and Bloomberg report a strike hit Saudi Aramco's Riyadh headquarters, unconfirmed by Saudi authorities, as Riyadh's cabinet vowed Houthis will face 'consequences' and Turkey's Erdogan pledged support, Al Arabiya and the Times of Israel report.

item.title: Issue 88 — Saudi-led coalition intercepts a Houthi missile at Riyadh as airlines scrap more Saudi flights
item.description: Iran's foreign ministry said it needs more time to answer Washington's counter-offer on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Reuters and Al Arabiya report, a day after Tehran called the earlier US reply 'insufficient'.

item.title: Issue 87 — Iran says the US response to its Hormuz reopening plan was 'insufficient'
item.description: Iran's security chief called Washington's response to its Hormuz reopening plan "insufficient," gCaptain, Al Arabiya and Reuters report, as US forces disabled another cargo vessel breaching Iran shipping limits.

item.title: Issue 86 — Taiwan earmarks a record NT$1.1 trillion for its 2027 defense budget
item.description: Taiwan earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion for its 2027 defense budget, citing deterrence, Deutsche Welle and the Straits Times report, after President Trump pressed Taipei to pay more for US protection.

item.title: Issue 85 — Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes Panama near the canal route, triggering tsunami warnings
item.description: A magnitude 7.6-7.7 earthquake struck Panama near the canal route on Friday, triggering tsunami warnings across six countries and an airport evacuation, MercoPress, the Associated Press, CBC News, Al Jazeera and Euronews report, with no confirmed canal disruption yet.

item.title: Issue 84 — US imposes fresh sanctions on tankers in Iran's shadow fleet
item.description: The US Treasury sanctioned more tankers and firms tied to Iran's shadow fleet as Strait of Hormuz transits fell to their lowest level in over two months, Reuters, gCaptain, Al Arabiya, the Hindu and Business Standard report, while Secretary of State Rubio said Iran has "lost complete control" of the strait.

item.title: Issue 83 — Brazil heads to an Oct 25 runoff as Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula in the first round
item.description: Iraq devalued its dinar by roughly 13% as the Strait of Hormuz's near-closure strains oil exports, Bloomberg and Al Arabiya report, while a tanker off Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles, UKMTO says.

item.title: Issue 82 — Saudi-backed Yemeni forces expel Houthi fighters from areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; Houthis claim fresh strikes on Saudi targets
item.description: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces pushed Houthi fighters from several areas near Bab el-Mandeb on Oct 5-6, AP and the Korea Herald report, while a Panama-flagged tanker was struck crossing the Strait of Hormuz, hurting a dozen crew including 11 Indians, gCaptain and Seatrade Maritime report.

item.title: Issue 81 — Yemen's government says its forces retook Mocha and secured the Bab el-Mandeb Strait; the Houthis deny any advance
item.description: BHP has asked Chile's labour inspectorate to mediate at Escondida, averting a strike that could have begun Tuesday, Rio Times and MINING.COM report, as Centinela's separate dispute also enters five-day mediation.

item.title: Issue 80 — Gulf oil exports rebound to pre-war levels even as tanker attacks continue and Iran weighs a harder response
item.description: QatarEnergy extended its LNG force majeure into November as European gas storage tracks toward just 75-78% of capacity, Bloomberg and Euronews report; JERA's CEO warns LNG prices still have room to climb.

item.title: Issue 79 — G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel reserves as a fifth tanker is struck in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: US diesel held near $6.37/gallon Friday, just under its $6.52 record, even after G7 leaders pledged an IEA-coordinated release of up to 100 million barrels over four months, Bloomberg and Al Jazeera report.

item.title: Issue 78 — Trump calls renewed bombing of Iran after the midterms “possible”; Iran's Revolutionary Guard calls him an “inveterate liar”
item.description: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports and PetroChina cancelled most of its October gasoline and jet fuel cargoes, Reuters reports; Bloomberg reports ship-fuel waits of one to two weeks at Zhoushan, China's main bunkering hub.

item.title: Issue 77 — Iran's UN delegation left New York Monday with no deal; Trump says “we blow them up or make a deal”
item.description: Saudi Arabia restarted Red Sea exports from Yanbu after a 17-day halt, its main route around Hormuz; ICE Brent settled at $97.46 on Sept 30, with no deal yet on Hormuz.

item.title: Issue 76 — Brent slides below $100 as Mideast oil exports near pre-war levels, even as Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz reopening offer
item.description: Oil's slide below $100 rippled quickly into cost-sensitive markets: the Baltic Dry Index fell to its lowest close since early September and India's Sensex fell for a second session, even as Adani Ports defied the broader selloff with a 4.5% rally.

item.title: Issue 75 — Iran leans into its Hormuz campaign as transits rebound to 132 a week, and its second drone-seizure claim shifts again
item.description: Monday's Hormuz-driven oil spike rippled through Indian equities: the Sensex slid to a six-month low and IRB Infrastructure hit a fresh 52-week low, even as Escondida's copper-mine standoff and Freeport's delayed Grasberg recovery kept metals markets on edge.

item.title: Issue 74 — Iran's parliament speaker vows Hormuz stays shut as IRGC claims a second US drone seizure and Trump still expects talks this week
item.description: Brent jumped back to $105.76 Monday morning, up 1.38% and briefly topping $106, as Iran's parliament speaker vowed Hormuz stays shut and a fresh, disputed drone-seizure claim added to the sense diplomacy is stalling even as Trump says he still expects talks this week.

item.title: Issue 73 — Trump formally rejects Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, calling it 'unacceptable' as officials eye strikes after the midterms
item.description: BHP is bringing Escondida, the world's largest copper mine, back online in stages after a fatal accident — layering a fresh disruption onto Grasberg's shortfall and keeping Comex copper pinned near its record $6.83/lb even as this week's session eased.

item.title: Issue 72 — Iran offers seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz as Trump reportedly rejects it, eyeing decisive action after the midterms
item.description: Markets read this week's diplomacy first through oil: Brent eased 1.3% to $105.26 and the Sensex rebounded 315 points Friday on hope Iran's seven-day Hormuz offer would hold — before word of Washington's reported rejection even spread.

item.title: Issue 71 — Iranian strike kills Indian seafarer aboard the Cape Dao as Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran and US-Iran talks float a 60-day Hormuz ceasefire roadmap
item.description: The Hormuz fatality rippled straight into India's own markets: the Sensex crashed 1,247.71 points and the Nifty gave up 383.70 as Thursday's oil spike wiped out Wednesday's full rebound in a single session — a reminder how directly Gulf shipping risk now prices into Dalal Street.

item.title: Issue 37 — Bessent's "Economic D-Day" finally lands as "Operation Economic Outcast" — but Tehran gets a grace period, and Hormuz stays nearly empty
item.description: Brent's slide to $92.06 a barrel and the Sensex's 172-point retreat are Monday's real market verdict on the sanctions news — a pattern of "sell the headline" repeating from last week's rally, even as war-risk tanker premiums stay locked at 7.5-10% of hull value and TD3C Gulf-China tanker earnings hold above $520,000 a day regardless of what Washington announces.

item.title: Issue 36 — Iran's Rezaei threatens to halt every drop of Gulf oil as Bessent's “Economic D-Day” sanctions near their 2pm ET unveiling
item.description: Brent's 1.38% Monday dip to $93.09 and the Sensex's 172-point slide to 77,369.11 are the market's own hedge against a sanctions package that hasn't landed yet — a reversal of last week's 5%-plus rally that reads as traders pricing pure uncertainty into the hours before Bessent's 2pm ET unveiling, not any actual resolution, even as Drewry's WCI holds at $4,526 and war-risk tanker premiums stay locked at 7.5-10% of hull value.

item.title: Issue 35 — Iran loses its grip on Hormuz as traffic bleeds into the Omani lane, hours before Bessent's “Economic D-Day” sanctions land
item.description: Brent's climb to $94.39 a barrel and Drewry's WCI holding at $4,526 are the market's own verdict on Hormuz — freight and crude pricing keep the standoff priced in even as Kpler finds merchant traffic quietly rerouting through Oman's coastal lane to dodge Iran's shrinking zone of control.
